High fidelity modeling of pumped storage units for optimal operation of a
multi-energy co-generation system
Ganggang Liang a, Hao Zhanga,b,∗, Chenxi Lia, Xin Wua, Pengcheng Guoa,b,∗∗, Haipeng Nana
a School of Water Resources and Hydroelectric Engineering, Xi’an University of Technology, Xi’an 710048, China

A B S T R A C T
Pumped storage, as the storage technology with the largest installed capacity and mature technology, plays
a key regulation role in the multi-energy co-generation system. The core of regulation accuracy is the high-
fidelity modeling of pumped storage. This paper improves the insufficiency of the conventional pumped storage
model (CPSM) in exaggerating the flexibility of pumped storage units by setting up non-operable operating
condition regions, and incorporates the condition switching loss into the model consideration, on the basis
of which a high fidelity pumped storage model (HFPSM) is established. Secondly, a multi-objective function
of the operation model is set from the consideration of economy, environmental protection and stability, and
a engineering application level optimal operation model of wind power-photovoltaic-thermal power-pumped
storage multi-energy co-generation system based on HFPSM is proposed. Thirdly, two research indicators,
the thermal power volatility indicator and the pumped storage unit utilization rate, are proposed. Fourthly,
combined with examples, the effects of CPSM and HFPSM on the optimized operation of the system are
investigated. It is found that adding four 50MW pumped storage units to the system can reduce the total
operating cost by 10.34% and the environmental cost by 83.61%. The optimization of the high fidelity model
is better under the premise of ensuring safe, stable and efficient operation of the system. Optimizing the number
of unit startups and shutdowns for the high fidelity model to 25.8% of the conventional model. Finally, by
exploring the optimal operation of a multi-energy co-generation system with different pumped storage installed
capacities, it is found that the proposed high fidelity model makes the optimization results more in line with
the actual operation. The flexibility of the pumped storage units no longer increases with the increase of
installed capacity, which provides a reference for the planning of the storage capacity in the multi-energy
co-generation system.
1. Introduction
With the depletion of fossil fuels and growing concern about the
impact on the environment, accelerating the development of renew-
able energy has become an inevitable choice for energy transforma-
tion ( Wang et al. , 2023a ; Mahfoud et al. , 2023 ). Renewable energy
generation has the characteristics of stochasticity, intermittency and
difficulty in scheduling, large-scale use of renewable energy generation
brings new challenge to the power system ( Daneshvar et al., 2020).
The inclusion of storage in the power system can provide greater
flexibility for the system, stabilize the volatility of renewable energy,
promote the consumption of renewable energy, and to some extent
eliminate the negative impacts of the large-scale use of renewable
energy. Pumping storage as the largest installed capacity, the most
mature technology of energy storage technology, is the focus of the

fectiveness of the adjustable speed pumped-storage hydropower plants
device by adding various numerical studies on the penetration factor of
wind power plants. Liang et al. (2020) investigated the optimal opera-
tion of an island microgrid containing wind, photovoltaic and diesel
generators using seawater pumped storage power station as energy
storage equipment. Despite the fact that many fruitful works have been
accomplished by scholars for the optimal operation of multi-energy co-
generation system, some minor problems have been identified. There
is a slight lack of accurate research for operational modeling, espe-
cially for pumped storage, the regulator in multi-energy co-generation
system. In the above references, the modeling for pumped storage
unit is relatively simplified, the model does not take into account the
actual operating characteristics of the unit and the losses of the unit’s
switching of operating conditions. Meanwhile, most of the mentioned
studies are hour-level optimization operation models, there is a lack of
engineering application level optimization operation models for smaller
time scales.
In the background of energy revolution in recent years, the de-
velopment of renewable energy is becoming more and more rapid.
China is one of the representatives, both the annual renewable energy
installed capacity and the total installed capacity of renewable energy
ranked first in the world. The energy regulation model proposed in this
paper can significantly improve the consumption of renewable energy,
meanwhile, accurately quantify the regulation capacity of pumped
storage. In some areas of western China, the installed capacity of
renewable energy is more than 70%, and it is urgent to have an accurate
and detailed energy regulation model. Secondly, pumped storage is an
important component as a regulator of multi-energy co-generation, and
the existing models are not detailed enough in describing the pumped
storage regulation model. Therefore, it is of great engineering interest
to study the optimal operation of multi-energy co-generation system
based on high fidelity modeling of pumped storage.
To address the abovementioned issues, in this paper, an engineering
application level optimization operation model of wind power (WP)-
photovoltaic (PV)-thermal power (TP)-pumped storage (PS) multi-
energy co-generation system based on pumped storage high fidelity
modeling is proposed with the contributions shown below.
• This paper accurately describes the operating range of pumped
storage units by setting the non-operable operating condition
regions in combination with the actual operating characteristics
of pumped storage units.
• This paper considers the unit combinations while accurately
quantifying the time loss and power loss when the units switch
operating conditions. Based on this, a high fidelity energy regu-
lation model for pumped storage units is proposed.
• From the consideration of economy, environmental protection
and stability, a multi-objective function is set for the operation
model.
• The example results show that the proposed high fidelity energy
regulation model reduces the number of pumped storage units
operating condition switching by 74.2% compared with the con-
ventional model under the premise of ensuring the safe and stable
operation of the system.
The remainder of the study is structured as follows. Section 2
introduces a engineering application level optimal operation model
of multi-energy co-generation system based on pumped storage high
fidelity modeling; Section 3 describes the basics of the simulation
example; Section 4 introduces the results of the simulation; Section 5
presents the conclusions and future work.
2. Optimal operation model
The multi-objective optimal operation of a multi-energy
co-generation system is a substantial problem, by utilizing the coupling
mechanism of each energy source in space and time, to realize multi-
energy complementarity and achieve a high proportion of renewable
energy consumption while taking into account the system stability,
safety and other operational objectives. In this paper, the multi-energy
co-generation system consists of power grid, customer load, WP, PV,
TP and PS, as shown in Fig. 1. WP, PV and TP are responsible for
power production and supplying energy to the customers through the
power grid. Pumped storage acts as a regulator of the power generation
system, regulating the energy of the grid by pumping and discharging
water for power generation to achieve the effect of peak-cutting and
valley-filling.
2.1. High fidelity modeling of PS
The research uses pumped storage units as risk management energy
storage devices for multi-energy co-generation system, modeled as
follow.
The operating range of the unit is a critical factor in the optimized
operation model. In the previous optimized operation model, CPSM sets
the operating condition can be any point between the rated generating
power and the rated pumping power, which is inconsistent with the
actual operating characteristics of the pumped storage unit. When the
pumped storage unit generates electricity at small output, the unit
is extremely unstable under the action of hydraulic and mechanical
factors, operation in this state for a long time will cause damage to
the unit. In pumping condition, conventional pumped storage units can
only pump at rated condition and cannot change the pumping power.
Variable-speed pumped storage units also only change power within
a certain range. Since most pumped storage units are conventional
pumped storage units, the research object of this paper is conventional
pumped storage units. This paper proposes to set the non-operable
operating condition region of pumped storage units in the model to
improve the previous CPSM. For expressing the state of pumped storage
power station and each unit, binary variables are introduced as state
indicators, when the value of the power generation condition state
indicator is 1, it indicates that the pumped storage unit is releasing
water for power generation, when its value is 0, the pumped storage
unit is not generating power. similarly, the pumping condition indicator
and the pumped storage power station state indicator are set. The

By changing the installed capacity of pumped storage connected
to the multi-energy co-generation system, the optimal operation of
multi-energy co-generation systems with different installed capacities
of pumped storage was investigated. It is found that the indicators of TP
volatility rates, carbon emission costs and environmental benefits did
not always continue to decrease with the increase in installed capacity
of PS units, but fluctuated at a certain level of increase in pumped
storage capacity. This is due to the fact that the HFPSM corrects the
inadequacy of the CPSM’s exaggerated description of pumped storage
flexibility. The flexibility of the pumped storage units no longer in-
creases with the increase of installed capacity, and the optimization
results are more in line with the actual operation. So, the proposed
HFPSM provides a reference basis for energy storage capacity planning
in multi-energy co-generation systems.
In this paper, the economic objectives include various costs of
system operation, but do not include the construction costs of the power
station. Therefore, in the study of changing the installed capacity of
pumped storage, there is no obvious optimal pumped storage capacity
in terms of economy. The pumped storage capacity that is relatively
friendly to the system can only be judged by combining various in-
dicators to be 50–60 MW. In future studies, the construction cost of
the power station should be fully considered and the model should be
described more comprehensively.
